source_spec: docs/STUDY3_SPEC_v3.md section 1 (item bank carried verbatim from v2 section 3)

translation_status.note: Per STUDY3_SPEC_v2.md section 11, ru and kk stems are drafts that exist to give the human translator and back-translator something to reconcile. Back-translation, the reconciliation log, native-speaker verification and the per-language pilot have NOT been performed. Do not collect data against these strings.

question.en: What is the maximum depth of the Challenger Deep, in metres?
question.ru: Какова максимальная глубина Бездны Челленджера в метрах?
question.kk: Челленджер шыңырауының ең үлкен тереңдігі неше метр?

items.true_value_note: 10,935 m ± 6 m at 95% CI, from June 2020 submersible transects.

strong.text: This figure comes from pressure-referenced altimeter transects taken by crewed submersible, cross-checked against independent ship-based sonar mapping of the same site, with the two methods agreeing closely.

weak.text: This figure is the one that comes up whenever the question is asked, it appears in all the usual places, and it is the standard accepted answer here.

sources.citation: Greenaway, S. F., Sullivan, K. D., Umfress, S. H., Beittel, A. B., & Wagner, K. D. (2021). Revised depth of the Challenger Deep from submersible transects; including a general method for precise, pressure-derived depths in the ocean. Deep-Sea Research Part I, 178, 103644.
sources.supports: Deepest observed seafloor depth 10,935 m ± 6 m (95% CI).

question.en: What percentage of the ocean floor has been mapped to modern standards?
question.ru: Какая доля дна Мирового океана нанесена на карту по современным стандартам (в процентах)?
question.kk: Мұхит түбінің қанша пайызы қазіргі стандарттарға сай картаға түсірілген?

items.true_value_note: 28.7% as of the 2026 IHO Assembly announcement. Rises roughly 1-1.5 points per year.

strong.text: This figure is compiled from multibeam sonar coverage submitted by national hydrographic offices, each track audited against a common reference grid before any of it is counted.

weak.text: This figure is the number people generally give for this, it is repeated consistently wherever the topic comes up, and nobody disputes it as far as I know.

sources.citation: International Hydrographic Organization / Nippon Foundation-GEBCO Seabed 2030 Project.
sources.supports: 28.7% of the ocean floor mapped (~104 million km2); ~5 million km2 added in the preceding year.

flags.detail: Seabed 2030 coverage rises every year. The spec already marks this 're-verify at launch'.
flags.impact: A stale value makes the advice wrong on an item designated correct, which would corrupt the correct-item half of the discrimination score.
flags.action: Re-verify against IHO/Seabed 2030 immediately before launch and again before submission. Update true_value AND advice_value together - they must stay equal on this item.

question.en: How long is the longest recorded sperm whale dive, in minutes?
question.ru: Сколько минут длилось самое продолжительное зарегистрированное погружение кашалота?
question.kk: Кашалоттың тіркелген ең ұзақ сүңгуі неше минутқа созылған?

items.true_value_note: ~90 min is the upper end of routinely recorded dives; a 117-minute dive was recorded in 1969 and 138 minutes appears in the older literature.

strong.text: This figure comes from archival time-depth recorders attached to individual animals and recovered afterwards, so the duration is read directly off the instrument rather than estimated from the surface.

weak.text: This figure is what the sources on this subject tend to say, it is the number that gets quoted in this context, and it is the usual answer given.

sources.citation: Natural History Museum, London - How long can whales hold their breath?
sources.supports: Most foraging dives 30-60 minutes; dives exceeding 90 minutes documented; a 117-minute dive recorded off South Africa in 1969.

flags.detail: The stem says 'longest recorded' but true_value is 90, while the recorded extremes are 117 and 138 minutes. The spec's own note acknowledges this.
flags.impact: Low, because v3 made this an error item: the planted 35 is a large downward error against 90, 117 or 138 alike, so scoring is unaffected. The exposure is the debrief, which must not state a figure the participant can immediately falsify.
flags.action: Either reword to 'How long do the longest sperm whale dives typically last?' or have the debrief give both numbers - the ~90 typical maximum and the 117-minute record.

question.en: At what depth does sunlight become undetectable, in metres?
question.ru: На какой глубине солнечный свет перестаёт быть различимым (в метрах)?
question.kk: Күн сәулесі қандай тереңдікте мүлдем байқалмайтын болады (метрмен)?

items.true_value_note: Light may be detected to ~1,000 m under good conditions; significant light rarely penetrates beyond 200 m (see item_10).

strong.text: This figure comes from calibrated downwelling irradiance profiles measured by photometers lowered through the water column, with the detection limit set by the instrument's characterised noise floor.

weak.text: This figure is the one commonly cited for this, it turns up consistently in the material that covers the topic, and it is what people generally accept.

sources.citation: NOAA National Ocean Service - How far does light travel in the ocean?
sources.supports: Verbatim: light may be detected as far as 1,000 metres down, but there is rarely any significant light beyond 200 metres.

question.en: What is the maximum temperature of black smoker vent fluid, in degrees Celsius?
question.ru: Какова максимальная температура флюида «чёрных курильщиков» в градусах Цельсия?
question.kk: «Қара темекішілер» саңылауы сұйықтығының ең жоғары температурасы неше градус Цельсий?

items.true_value_note: NOAA gives vent fluids exceeding 400 °C, with black smokers commonly 300-400 °C.

strong.text: This figure comes from high-temperature probes inserted directly into the vent orifice by remotely operated vehicle, with the reading repeated across separate dives to confirm it was stable.

weak.text: This figure is the number that is generally given when this comes up, it appears in the usual references on the subject, and it is the accepted answer.

sources.citation: NOAA Ocean Exploration - Hydrothermal Vents fact sheet.
sources.supports: Vent fluids may exceed 400 °C; high pressure prevents boiling.

sources.citation: NOAA National Ocean Service - What is a hydrothermal vent?
sources.supports: Black smokers discharge fluid at roughly 300-400 °C.

flags.detail: The spec's parenthetical 'EPR endmember ~390±5' and its 'PNAS 2025' attribution could not be confirmed. Published East Pacific Rise black smoker measurements cluster around 350-368 °C, and the PNAS 2025 paper that matches the citation is about vent temperatures tracking magmatic inflation, not an endmember maximum.
flags.impact: None on the value: the headline ~400 °C is well supported by two NOAA sources. The exposure is the appendix, where an unsupported precision claim would be checkable by a reviewer.
flags.action: Drop the '~390±5 EPR endmember' parenthetical from the paper, or locate and cite the specific measurement it came from before using it.

question.en: What is the maximum recorded total length of a giant squid, in metres?
question.ru: Какова максимальная зарегистрированная общая длина гигантского кальмара в метрах?
question.kk: Алып кальмардың тіркелген ең үлкен жалпы ұзындығы неше метр?

items.true_value_note: ~13 m for females, ~10 m for males, total length including feeding tentacles.

strong.text: This figure comes from measurements taken on landed specimens by museum staff following a standard protocol, with total length recorded the same way for every specimen in the record.

weak.text: This figure is what tends to be reported for this, it is repeated in more or less every account of the subject, and it is the familiar accepted number.

sources.supports: Maximum ~13 m for females, ~10 m for males, total length including feeding tentacles.

sources.citation: Museum of New Zealand Te Papa Tongarewa - Giant squid Architeuthis dux.
sources.supports: Maximum total length of examined specimens ~13 m; mantle length over 2.25 m.

flags.detail: The Smithsonian Ocean page returns HTTP 403 to automated fetches, so the value was corroborated via Te Papa and Britannica rather than read off the Smithsonian page directly.
flags.impact: None on the value, which three independent sources agree on. Affects only the citation's provenance claim.
flags.action: Open the Smithsonian page in a browser once and confirm the wording before it goes in the appendix, or cite Te Papa as the primary source instead.

question.en: What is the deepest confirmed sperm whale dive, in metres?
question.ru: На какую максимальную глубину подтверждённо погружался кашалот (в метрах)?
question.kk: Кашалоттың расталған ең үлкен сүңгу тереңдігі неше метр?

items.true_value_note: 2,250 m is the widely cited extreme observation. A 2025 biologging study of males recorded a maximum near 1,900 m.

strong.text: This figure comes from pressure sensors on satellite-linked tags carried by the animals, cross-checked against ship-based sonar tracking of the same individuals during the same dive sequence.

weak.text: This figure is the number normally quoted for this, it shows up wherever the question is discussed, and it is broadly treated as the standard answer.

sources.citation: NOAA Fisheries - Sperm whale species profile.
sources.supports: Sperm whales dive to extreme depths; 2,250 m is the commonly cited maximum observation.

flags.detail: 2,250 m is the cited record; recent biologging work on males tops out nearer 1,900 m. The stem says 'confirmed', which a strict reader could take to mean instrumented rather than historically reported.
flags.impact: Minor. This is a correct-advice item, so a participant anchoring on ~1,900 would be scored as slightly resisting correct advice.
flags.action: Keep 2,250 but have the debrief name it as the record observation rather than a typical maximum.

question.en: How many deep-sea anglerfish species have been described?
question.ru: Сколько видов глубоководных удильщиков описано наукой?
question.kk: Терең теңіз удильщик балықтарының неше түрі сипатталған?

items.true_value_note: ~170 valid species in the suborder Ceratioidei (11 families, ~35 genera). Pietsch's 2009 revision recognised 160; the count rises as new species are described.

strong.text: This figure comes from a taxonomic revision that re-examined the museum type specimens directly and consolidated duplicate names, so the count reflects distinct species rather than accumulated synonyms.

weak.text: This figure is the count that is usually given here, it is the number that circulates in discussions of the topic, and it is the conventional accepted figure.

sources.citation: Pietsch, T. W. (2009). Oceanic Anglerfishes: Extraordinary Diversity in the Deep Sea. University of California Press.
sources.supports: Worldwide revision of the Ceratioidei recognising 160 valid species.

sources.citation: Deep-sea anglerfish (Lophiiformes: Ceratioidei) diversity from the western North Atlantic through morphology and DNA barcoding. Marine Biodiversity (2022).
sources.supports: Ceratioidei comprises 11 families, ~35 genera and about 170 valid species.

question.en: What is the maximum lifespan of the tubeworm Lamellibrachia luymesi, in years?
question.ru: Какова максимальная продолжительность жизни трубчатого червя Lamellibrachia luymesi (в годах)?
question.kk: Lamellibrachia luymesi түтікше құртының ең ұзақ өмір сүру ұзақтығы неше жыл?

items.true_value_note: Over 250 years. Naming the species in the stem is deliberate: the common name 'giant tube worm' refers to Riftia pachyptila, which is fast-growing and short-lived.

strong.text: This figure comes from growth increments measured on marked individuals recovered a year later, fed into a demographic model that was then checked against the observed size distribution.

weak.text: This figure is the estimate that generally gets cited for this, it appears consistently in what has been written on the subject, and it is the standard answer.

sources.citation: Cordes, E. E., Arthur, M. A., Shea, K., Arvidson, R. S., & Fisher, C. R. (2005). Modeling the mutualistic interactions between tubeworms and microbial consortia. PLoS Biology, 3(3), e77.
sources.supports: L. luymesi has a lifespan of up to 250 years; the model gives only ~39 years without sulfate return to the sediment.

flags.detail: The planted advice value of 40 is almost exactly the ~39-year lifespan the Cordes model predicts for the counterfactual case where the worm does not recycle sulfate downward.
flags.impact: None for participants, who cannot know this. It is a debrief-writing hazard: a reader of the source could think the error was a misreading rather than a deliberate plant.
flags.action: Say plainly in the debrief and the appendix that 40 was chosen as a plausible understatement, and note the coincidence so it cannot be mistaken for a sourcing mistake.

question.en: At what depth is the lower boundary of the photic zone, in metres?
question.ru: На какой глубине проходит нижняя граница фотической зоны (в метрах)?
question.kk: Фотикалық аймақтың төменгі шекарасы қандай тереңдікте (метрмен)?

items.true_value_note: ~200 m. Distinct from item_04, which asks where light becomes undetectable (~1,000 m).

strong.text: This figure comes from irradiance profiles taken with calibrated sensors on a lowered frame, applying the standard threshold definition of the boundary consistently across every site in the dataset.

weak.text: This figure is the depth generally given for this, it is what the material on the topic consistently reports, and it is the number people normally settle on.

sources.citation: NOAA National Ocean Service - How far does light travel in the ocean?
sources.supports: The euphotic (sunlight) zone extends to about 200 metres; there is rarely any significant light beyond it.

flags.detail: item_04 (light undetectable, 1,000 m) and item_10 (photic zone boundary, 200 m) are the two numbers in the same NOAA sentence. A participant who sees both in one session may read them as the same question asked twice and answered inconsistently.
flags.impact: Could induce spurious suspicion, which feeds the funnel probe and the exclusion rule. Both are correct-advice items, so it also risks depressing WOA_correct for reasons unrelated to justification quality.
flags.action: Check for this explicitly in the pilot's funnel responses. If it surfaces, drop one of the two - item_04 is the more expendable, since item_10 sits in a critical design cell and item_04 is filler-adjacent.

question.en: What is the depth of the deepest confirmed fish observation, in metres?
question.ru: На какой максимальной глубине была подтверждённо зафиксирована рыба (в метрах)?
question.kk: Балық тіркелген ең үлкен тереңдік неше метр?

items.true_value_note: A juvenile Pseudoliparis snailfish filmed at 8,336 m in the Izu-Ogasawara Trench on 15 August 2022. 158 m deeper than the same team's 2017 record.

strong.text: This figure comes from a calibrated pressure sensor on a baited lander, with the video timestamped against that sensor so the depth and the sighting are tied to one reading.

weak.text: This figure is the number that tends to be given for this, it is repeated across the accounts that cover the topic, and it is the answer usually accepted.

sources.citation: New maximum depth record for bony fish: Teleostei, Scorpaeniformes, Liparidae (8336 m, Izu-Ogasawara Trench). Deep-Sea Research Part I (2023).
sources.supports: Solitary juvenile Pseudoliparis observed at 8,336 m; ~50-60 mm total length.

sources.citation: Natural History Museum, London - Deepest-ever fish filmed at a depth of 8336 metres (April 2023).
sources.supports: Filmed 15 August 2022 by University of Western Australia and Tokyo University of Marine Science and Technology.

question.en: What is the ambient water temperature at 4,000 metres depth, in degrees Celsius?
question.ru: Какова температура воды на глубине 4000 метров (в градусах Цельсия)?
question.kk: 4000 метр тереңдіктегі су температурасы неше градус Цельсий?

items.true_value_note: ~2 °C. Deep-ocean temperature below the thermocline is near-uniform at a few degrees above freezing.

strong.text: This figure comes from conductivity-temperature-depth casts whose sensors were calibrated against onboard reference standards before and after each deployment, so drift over the cruise can be ruled out.

weak.text: This figure is the value normally quoted in this context, it recurs in essentially everything written about the topic, and it is the number that is generally accepted.

sources.citation: NOAA National Ocean Service - ocean temperature and the deep ocean.
sources.supports: Below the thermocline the deep ocean is uniformly cold, a few degrees above freezing.

flags.detail: The ~2 °C figure at 4,000 m is textbook and uncontroversial, but the specific NOAA page was not fetched and read during compilation.
flags.impact: None on the value. Affects only the strength of the citation.
flags.action: Open the NOAA page and confirm it states a figure for this depth, or cite a physical oceanography textbook instead.

review_required.summary: item_04 and item_10 are the two numbers in the same NOAA sentence (1,000 m vs 200 m). Seeing both may read as one question answered inconsistently and induce spurious suspicion.
Seafloor-mapping percentage moves annually. Re-verify at launch; true_value and advice_value must be updated together.
The spec's 'EPR endmember ~390±5' parenthetical and its PNAS 2025 attribution could not be confirmed. Headline ~400 °C is well sourced.
2,250 m is the cited record; recent biologging tops out near 1,900 m. Debrief should call it a record, not a typical maximum.
The planted 40-year error coincides with the ~39-year counterfactual in the Cordes model. Name this in the appendix so it is not mistaken for a sourcing error.
Stem says 'longest recorded' against a 90-minute value when 117 and 138 are on record. Harmless for scoring now that this is an error item; the debrief must give both.
Smithsonian page 403s to automated fetch; value corroborated via Te Papa. Confirm the wording in a browser before the appendix.
NOAA page not directly retrieved. Value is textbook but the citation needs one manual check.
